messages.subject: A third reactive table, based on two previous
messages.subject_clean: A third reactive table, based on two previous
messages.body_plain:
Im trying Shiny and building a simple app to choose different values from two datasets, and the compare these values. See the app so far at :

http://spark.rstudio.com/energidk/lasse/

(It takes a little time to load the data)

The top table are future values, and the lower table is historical values. I would like a third table under does two, that can do simple calculations based on the day you choose. For example:

I choose 2 days ahead, which means that in the box:  "Number of days to view, max 14:" is set equal to 2. Now I choose 7 historical days to compare with.

Now I would like a third reactive table under these two, that simply does a percentage calculation, so:

          Columns....
Row 1: day 2 values / day 1 historical
Row 2: day 2 values / day 2 historical
Row 3: day 2 values / day 3 historical... etc.

My Shiny code so far:

ui.R

library(shiny)

# Define UI for dataset viewer application
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  # Application title
  headerPanel("Germany Balance"),

  # Sidebar with controls to select a dataset and specify the number
  # of observations to view
  sidebarPanel(
    selectInput("dataset", "Choose Number of Days Ahead:",
                choices = c("Base", "Peak", "Off-Peak")),

    numericInput("obs", "Number of days to view, max 14:", 7)

  ,
    # Slider
    selectInput("datahis", "Choose Number of Historical Days:",
                choices = c("Base", "Peak", "Off-Peak")),

    numericInput("obshis", "Number of days to view:", 7)
),

  # Show a summary of the dataset and an HTML table with the requested
  # number of observations
  mainPanel(

    tableOutput("view"),
    tableOutput("hisview")
  )
))

server.R

# Server
library(shiny)
library(plyr)

# Define server logic required to summarize and view the selected dataset
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  # Return the requested dataset
  datasetInput <- reactive({
    switch(input$dataset,
           "Base" = base,
           "Peak" = peak,
           "Off-Peak" = offpeak)
  })

  # Show the first "n" observations
  output$view <- renderTable({
    head(datasetInput(), n = input$obs)
  })

  datahisInput <- reactive({
    switch(input$datahis,
           "Base" = h_base,
           "Peak" = h_peak,
           "Off-Peak" = h_offpeak)
  })

  # Show the first "n" observations
  output$hisview <- renderTable({
    head(datahisInput(), n = input$obshis)
  })
})

# getting data from FTP-server and manipulation it into two frames, a historical and predictive.

messages.subject: Re: Commercial Shiny Server Timeline and Features?
messages.subject_clean: Commercial Shiny Server Timeline and Features?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Joe,

Thank you for all your work on Shiny. I fully agree with what Aaron Horowitz said.

I read you planned to launch a beta version of the commercial version of Shiny Server: I was wondering if that version will allow a " subscription-based hosting service for Shiny" (just like beta acess to Shiny applications deployment from http://glimmer.rstudio.com:8787). If so, have you got an idea of the timeline ?

To my mind, the main requirements for a commercial use of Shiny are multiple and secure access indeed.

Thank you again,

Dominique

Le mardi 23 avril 2013 15:43:25 UTC+2, Aaron Horowitz a écrit :
> Hi Shiny Devs. (Winston, Joe, etc.),
>
> First of all, I want to to thank you for building this wonderful web framework. I've attempted to work with other frameworks in the past, and found them far more difficult to implement and use, and ultimately it was easier to just avoid them altogether. Shiny, on the other hand, has been incredibly straightforward to use and we've been able to make some powerful apps out of it already.  Notably, it's allowed me to use the analytic power of R in situations where other, more clunky, solutions were in place and create a whole lot more impact with my clients/colleagues. SO BIG KUDOS TO YOU AND THE TEAM!
>
> For me to make full use of the software and really take it to the next level, we'll need some good and powerful authentication (all of my data is highly confidential and there's concerns in my company that web-sockets can be hacked a little easier than alternatives) and other back-end solutions to make sure the proper infrastructure is in place to share our Shiny apps outside of the intranet.
>
> I know you have discussed elsewhere on the forum that authentication will be part of the commercial version. Are there any other features you plan to implement that you can share with us?  Would this be a proper place to make requests for the types of features we'd hope for out of the commercial version of this software? And lastly, any ideas on when you'll be offering this or when you'll start building it up beyond the beta?
>
> Obviously you're free to leave me/us out of this (I don't want to jeopardize you making some real money off of all the work y'all have done!), but I'd--maybe others too?--certainly love to know!
>
> Regards,
> Aaron

messages.subject: documentation?
messages.body_plain:
Hi folks -

I am new at Shiny, and love the concept!  However, I'm having a tough time, even with the tutorials, really digesting how to use it.  For instance, I have a simple app I am trying to build,
that takes data from a user uploaded csv and performs various statistics on the data.  I can see in the tutorials how to upload a data set (it works) and how to plot data (ie, histogram example) but I cannot figure out how to plot the data I just uploaded - ie, how do I reference it once it's been read with read.csv?

Which leads me to ask - is there any more formal documentation of Shiny, beyond what's in the tutorials on Github?  (one can hope...)

Also, I am assuming Shiny can make use of R libraries and all the standard functions calls - correct?

Thank you.. and please go easy on this newbie :)

Cynthia

messages.body_plain:
Sorry for the delay in replying. For now here's a replacement S4 method, just include this in your server.R:

setMethod("toJSON", "numeric",

           function(x, container =  isContainer(x, asIs, .level), collapse = "\n", digits = 10, ...,

                      .level = 1L, .withNames = length(x) > 0 && length(names(x)) > 0,

                        .na = "null", .escapeEscapes = TRUE, pretty = FALSE, asIs = NA) {

            if(any(is.infinite(x)))

              warning("non-fininte values in numeric vector may not be approriately represented in JSON")

             tmp = formatC(x, digits = digits)

             if(any(nas <- is.na <http://is.na>(x)))

                 tmp[nas] = .na

             if(container) {

                if(.withNames)

                   paste(sprintf("{%s", collapse), paste(dQuote(names(x)), tmp, sep = ": ", collapse = sprintf(",%s", collapse)),

                                   sprintf("%s}", collapse))

                else
                   paste("[", paste(tmp, collapse = ", "), "]")

             } else

               tmp
           })

messages.subject_clean: "Maximum upload size exceeded" when upload csv data
messages.body_plain:
By default, Shiny limits file uploads to 5MB per file. You can modify this limit by using the shiny.maxRequestSize option. For example, adding options(shiny.maxRequestSize=30*1024^2) to the top of server.R would increase the limit to 30MB.

I talked to the googleVis guys during the useR conference and we intend to merge my code with their package.

For the columns parameter (which is optional), if you specify it, then you must provide a list of column() calls, one per variable in your dataframe.

I'm not familiar with motion chart options but with my bindings as they stand I think you need to have the variable you want as the id as the first variable in the data frame, and the second one is time.

messages.subject_clean: controlling the size of layout elements
messages.body_plain:
You can add your own CSS to your ui.R. Here's a simple example:

tags$style(type="text/css", "#mytable { width: 450px }")

Just include that anywhere a UI component is allowed.

You can also use includeCSS.

I'm hoping to do a screencast on the contents of ui.R and how you can intermingle custom HTML/CSS/JS without dropping down to a .html file.

--

When ui.R generates HTML, it doesn't actually write anything to disk; it's just held in memory. If you'd like to see the HTML that's generated by ui.R, really the best way is to just do View Source in your browser when your app is running.

messages.subject: Re: sending RGL output to Shiny (non-interactively)
messages.body_plain:
I've just uploaded a patch to rgl to R-forge that lets it run without any active display.  Set options(rgl.useNULL=TRUE) (or set the RGL_USE_NULL environment variable to "true") before loading rgl, and it will not need a display.

The assumption of an active display was fairly widespread in the code, so there may be some spots I missed.  (And it's hard to spot errors in graphics code that doesn't display anything!)

There are a few limitations:  it won't update the modelMatrix or projMatrix components of par3d(), for example, and there's no frame buffer, so nothing involving reading pixels is available.  But it does run through its usual tests without crashing, and will produce WebGL output.

Duncan

messages.subject: Non-HTML5 browser options..?
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I have developed a few apps using Shiny and they work great in html5 browsers (Chrome, IE10, etc) but not so well in IE8 and IE9.

80% of the time the apps get stuck trying to load the server scripts, and the other times they will usually lock up on input changes.

This is using both my own Shiny Server instance and also the spark.rstudio.com <http://spark.rstudio.com> server.

I realize that IE8+9 don't support websockets (which Shiny needs) so I was just wondering if there are any other solutions which may work for these browsers..?

I am not sure if some sort of curl proxy could work (?)

This is such an excellent program it would be a shame if I can't use it till the rest of the world has migrated to html5 browsers :)

messages.subject: Re: Formatting Table
messages.body_plain:
Hey,

As the tables are standard html it is fairly easily to add some css styles to format it.

Have a look at this link: Formatting Tables <http://spark.rstudio.com/torbenm/tables/>

Just put your stylesheet in the www folder and add the tags$head and tags$link tags at the top of your ui.R file.

The standard renderTable has a class called .table-bordered so just use that in your css.

EG,

tags$head(
tags$title('Table Formatting'),
tags$link(rel = 'stylesheet', type = 'text/css', href = 'stylesheet.css')
),

messages.subject: Re: Non-HTML5 browser options..?
messages.body_plain:
After a bit of investigation I think I have solved my own problem with IE7+8+9 compatibility...

It seems that you need to put the browser into 'quirks mode' for Shiny to work OK..

Currently Shiny outputs IE7+8+9 'standards mode' using the doctype:

> <!DOCTYPE html>

However IE10 seems to be using the old quirks mode by default:

> <!DOCTYPE html PUBLIC "">

If I create my own template with the quirks mode doctype (using www instead of ui.R) then everything works great...!!

I am not sure how this may affect other browsers on different platforms but it would be worth investigating..

messages.subject: Re: Exposing dendrogram data to Javascript
messages.body_plain:
Mike, did you install the repo as an R package? You shouldn't need to look at the files at all unless you want to modify them.

if (!require("devtools"))
  install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("d3-heatmap", "jcheng5")

In your ui.R and server.R, make sure to library(heatmap) [I should probably change the name] so heatmapOutput and renderHeatmap can be found.

You can also play with it without writing your own Shiny app by calling heatmap::showHeatmap(x) where x is a numeric matrix.

messages.subject: Re: How to determine data loading progress in Shiny?
messages.subject_clean: How to determine data loading progress in Shiny?
messages.body_plain:
Tried it out and looks good!

My understanding is that since we need to feed it increments, this will mainly be useful when we have several slow steps (and can increment between them). If, for example, doing a database pull takes up almost all the time, then this isn't suitable as no progress can be updated during the pull (even if we can estimate the time the pull will take)? In any case, still very useful as even an arbitrary status bar set at 25% before the pull will give the user some illusion of progress.

You can determine the elapsed time in pure JavaScript if you wanted to; whenever that conditionalPanel condition is evaluated, run a function. This function will see if the busy status (presence/absence of shiny-busy CSS class on <html>) has changed since the last time. If it has changed from not-busy to busy, then save the current time. Then once every second or so (using setInterval) calculate the number of seconds since the start time, and update the progress message with that value.

messages.subject: How can I limit chart disable/fading on processing?
messages.subject_clean: How can I limit chart disable/fading on processing?
messages.body_plain:
When there is a user interaction which is intended to result in a changed chart, the chart fades presumably to indicate
to the user that there is some processing underway

I am trying to develop an app which polls a website every minute (for  an updated sports score) and potentially does some quite intensive processing on the results returned

 data <- reactive({

   invalidateLater(60000, session)

## poll url and produce a character vector 'results'

# process 'results' with end-product info including data.frame, df

return(info)
})

output$chart <- renderPlot({
# process data()$df  to produce chart
})

Currently, the processing of all the results takes about a minute so the chart gets redrawn and immediately fades away for re-processing
I would ideally like to limit the processing to take place only if length(results) differs between consecutive polls and then just add rows as necessary
to df. This would significantly reduce the time the chart is in processing-mode but I am not sure how to store and use the previous' results' and 'df'

Alternatively, is there a way to turn off the fading so that the chart remains fully visible other when redrawing is necessary?

cheers

Matt

DataTables has several configuration parameters and the rCharts wrapper to DataTables exposes all of them, so that you can customize your application easily.

If you have suggestions/comments/feedback, please post them on the github page for rCharts.

Best,
Ramnath

messages.subject: Re: DataTables and Shiny
messages.body_plain:
You can handle it just like sPaginationType. The key is to make sure that the R representation of the object results in the correct JSON. For example.

mytable <- dTable(iris, aaSorting = list(c(1, "desc")))

would display the table sorted descending on the first column.

If you do toJSON(list(c(1, "desc"))), you will get [[1, "desc"]].  So when in doubt, use fromJSON to figure out the correct representation in R.

I am toying with the idea of allowing configuration parameters to be input as either R objects or JSON directly, in which case, you could just copy the JSON required. But, this is scheduled for a later version.

Let me know if this addresses your question.

messages.subject_clean: Bike Share Shiny App and UTF-8 Encoding Errors
messages.body_plain:
I had earlier shared my work on visualizing NYC Bike Share network. Using a more general data source, I was able to create a Shiny App that can visualize bike sharing networks across the world.

Source: https://gist.github.com/ramnathv/6050562
Application: http://glimmer.rstudio.com/ramnathv/bikeshare

The only glitch I am running into is with regard to encoding. For some of the cities (especially with Spanish of French street names), the application quits without any meaningful error. When I test locally, I see the following message in the Chrome Console

WebSocket connection to 'ws://localhost:8100/' failed: Could not decode a text frame as UTF-8.

So, it seems to be an encoding issue. Now, in my R code, I tried to force convert data to UTF-8 using

bike = fromJSON(iconv(content(GET(url)), to = "UTF-8"))

But, that doesn't do the work, as the characters remain even after this statement.

So my question is what is the best way to deal with UTF-8 encoding errors. I have seen some solutions using JS, where the idea is to scrub the payload sent by server.R. But, I was more curious about R side solutions, as it would make my job easier.

Looking forward to comments/suggestions.

Best,
Ramnath

messages.subject: Re: Configuring the size of ggplot chart
messages.subject_clean: Configuring the size of ggplot chart
messages.body_plain:
This worked for me. The png is generated by ggsave using predefined dimensions.
The figure is displayed in browser using the current session height and width. The figure resizes dynamically with browser
If the figure is saved, the original predefined dimensions are maintained.

#-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#Full working script shown
#ui.R
library(shiny)
library(reshape)
library(ggplot2)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("ggplot figure test"),
  sidebarPanel(),
  mainPanel(imageOutput("figure")
    )))

#server.R
library(datasets)

shinyServer(function(input, output,session) {

output$figure <- renderImage({
  width  <- session$clientData$output_figure_width
  height <- session$clientData$output_figure_height
  p2 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg))+ geom_point()
  outfile <- "image.png"
  ggsave(outfile,p2,height=6, width=12,dpi=300)
  list(src = outfile, contentType = 'image/png', width = width, height = width/2, alt = "image")

},deleteFile = TRUE)
})
#-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

messages.subject: Re: change background color
messages.body_plain:
If you are using page with sidebar layout, you can add CSS tags to modify styles of specific elements of your app.
Try this (in ui.r)
        sidebarPanel
        (
            tags$head(
                tags$style("body {background-color: black; }")
            )
                 #Sidebar controls
                  )

I suggest placing all your style tags in a separate file and referencing it with tags$link inside tags$head. e.g:
tags$link(rel="stylesheet", type="text/css", href="styles.css")

messages.subject: Linked Statistical Data Analysis
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'd like to share a Shiny implementation.

I created http://stats.270a.info/

Paper/documentation on the whole thing at:

http://csarven.ca/linked-statistical-data-analysis

Basically the application utilizes federated SPARQL queries to gather
statistical observation values from different endpoints based only on
user's selections (independent, dependent variables, and reference
period). The Shiny application and server bridges the front-end Web user
interface with R on the server-side in order to compare statistical
observations, and stores analysis results in RDF for future research.

Source code at:

https://github.com/csarven/lsd-analysis

So, for instance, here is one analysis that's most likely not that
interesting, but it will give you an idea on how it works:

http://stats.270a.info/analysis/worldbank:SP.DYN.IMRT.IN/transparency:CPI2009/year:2009

Independent variable from World Bank
Dependent variable from Transparency International
Reference period year 2009

There is content negotiation going on for that URI, so if you are using
your Web browser, you'll probably get the .html (regular web UI)
serialization. However, if you requestion for RDF/XML, Turtle, or JSON,
you'll get those serializations e.g.:

curl -LH "Accept: application/rdf+xml"
http://stats.270a.info/analysis/worDYN.IMRT.IN/transparency:CPI2009/year:2009

Since there are way too many combinations, I don't pre-compute and store
them. Instead, I let the users take care of that. Every analysis that's
conducted is written to the RDF store. You can what was analysed so far:

http://stats.270a.info/sparql?query=SELECT+*+WHERE+{+%3Fs+a+%3Chttp%3A%2F%2Fstats.270a.info%2Fvocab%23Analysis%3E+}%0D%0A%0D%0A&default-graph-uri=&output=xml&stylesheet=%2Fxml-to-html-links.xsl <http://stats.270a.info/sparql?query=SELECT+*+WHERE+%7B+%3Fs+a+%3Chttp%3A%2F%2Fstats.270a.info%2Fvocab%23Analysis%3E+%7D%0D%0A%0D%0A&default-graph-uri=&output=xml&stylesheet=%2Fxml-to-html-links.xsl>

Currently, the application lets you select from the following Linked
Datasets:

* World Bank (only Indicators)
* European Central Bank
* OECD
* FAO of UN
* Transparency International

It can be extended simply by adding more query endpoints.

I plan to add IMF, BIS, and Eurostat soon.

See also: http://270a.info/

I still have *a lot* of things to iron out - I would only call this
version 0.1 - but all feedback is most welcome!

I'll follow up with bite size feedback and questions in separate emails.

And, thanks again to everyone for helping me get through Shiny and
server basics... well, still learning :)

-Sarven
http://csarven.ca/#i

messages.subject: Reactivity vs. Static data
messages.body_plain:
I'm not sure if this is entirely possible, but I am attempting to build a dynamic distribution display tool. I have everything working as of right now but have hit a bit of a wall.

In the current version, the user selects a certain data distribution, a number of observations to take, the number of sample means to take, and the sample size for the each sample mean. I then have two plots output, the first just showing the sample distribution, and the second showing the distribution of the sample mean at that point. However, the sample mean distribution is "too reactive". By that I mean, every time the number of sample means changes, it starts the sampling process over. Instead, I would like it to take 1 sample of say "n" observations and then stay put. At this point, as the number of sample means changes, each sample comes from the dataset (not generate a new data set to sample from for each concurrent sample mean calculation. That result should be stored into a vector or data frame, and the second plot will build upon itself as the number of sample means increases.

I have not deployed this yet so I will post the raw code below to hopefully give a better idea of what I'm doing.

ui.R

library(shiny)

# UI definition for distribution tool
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  # title
  headerPanel("Distribution Visualization Tool"),

  # Sidebar for choosing distribution type, sample size, # of means, etc.
  sidebarPanel(
    radioButtons("dist", "Distribution type:",
                 list("Normal" = "norm",
                      "Uniform" = "unif",
                      "Log-normal" = "lnorm",
                      "Exponential" = "exp")),
    br(),

    sliderInput("n",
                "Number of observations:",
                value = 500,
                min = 1,
                max = 5000),

    # animation looping for number of sample means to take
    # note: interval controls the speed in ms between steps

    sliderInput("N",
                "Number of Sample Means:", 1,100,1,step=1,
                animate=animationOptions(interval=500, loop=T)),

    sliderInput("xbar.size",
                "Sample Size for Sample Mean:",
                value = 5,
                min = 1,
                max = 500)
  ),

  # Present information in 2 tabs: plot and data summary
  mainPanel(
    tabsetPanel(
      tabPanel("Plot", plotOutput("plot1"),plotOutput("plot2")),
      tabPanel("Summary", verbatimTextOutput("summary1"),verbatimTextOutput("summary2"))
    )
  )
))

server.R

library(shiny)

# server logic
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  #generate data from selected distribution
  data <- reactive({
    dist <- switch(input$dist,
                   norm = rnorm,
                   unif = runif,
                   lnorm = rlnorm,
                   exp = rexp,
                   rnorm)

    dist(input$n)
  })

####
this is the chunk of the code that I think will need to change
####

  means <- reactive({
    if(input$xbar.size<input$n){
    sample.means<-numeric(input$N)
    for(i in 1:input$N)
    sample.means[i]<-mean(sample(data(),input$xbar.size,FALSE))
    sample.means
   }
  })

  # Plot the underlying distribution on top, and the distribution
  # of the sample mean on bottom.
  output$plot1 <- renderPlot({
    dist <- input$dist
    n <- input$n

    hist(data(),
         main=paste("Observations: ",'r', dist, " ~ (",round(mean(data()),3),",",round(sd(data()),3),")", sep=''))
  })

  output$plot2 <- renderPlot({
    dist <- input$dist
    n <- input$n

    hist(means(),xlim=c(mean(data())-2*sd(data()),mean(data())+2*sd(data())),
         main=paste("Sample Means: Approximately ~ N(",round(mean(means()),3),",",round(sd(means()),3),")",sep=''))
  })

  # Generate a summary of the data
  output$summary1 <- renderPrint({
    summary(data())
  })

  output$summary2 <- renderPrint({
    summary(means())
  })

})

I'm not sure if there is a way to have selective reactivity for a reactive function, or a way to store static values from a reactive function as it changes for future accessing or what, but would appreciate any help anyone can offer.

Thanks in advance!

Jb

Oh, it was not clear that you wanted to keep previous values.

Here is one way you can do it:

#define a data set outside your server function, say allData.
allMeans <- NULL

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

#in your data function update this one:

  means <- reactive({
    if(input$xbar.size<input$n){
    sample.means<-numeric(input$N)
    for(i in 1:input$N)
    sample.means[i]<-mean(sample(data(),input$xbar.size,FALSE))

    allMeans <<- c(allMeans,sample.means)
    allMeans
   }
  })

This should do what you want. The problem is for a given user, this value will persist as long as the session does - even if the refresh. What you need to add is a button that will set allMeans to NULL when it is clicked.

There might be a simpler way to do this but this should work.

messages.body_plain:
I just checked it into the Shiny repository on GitHub. Use the instructions on the repo page <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny> to install the latest development build.

Once you have updated Shiny (and keep in mind that if you are doing this for Shiny Server, the development build of Shiny must be installed either by root or by the "shiny" user) then you can add a "session" parameter to your shinyServer function, then access session$request to get at the request. The request is an environment that matches the Rook API <https://github.com/jeffreyhorner/Rook#the-environment>, so custom HTTP headers are available as HTTP_<headername>, all caps.

Example:

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  print(session$request$HTTP_USER_AGENT)
})

messages.body_plain:
You could do the downloading and calculating directly in Shiny using `observe`, `invalidateLater`, and `reactiveValues`, but I doubt that would be the best approach. The problem with doing it directly in Shiny is that Shiny applications generally shut down when they're not being used. You'd most likely want to run the download and calculation as a separate script, that puts the resulting time series data in a .csv or .Rds or database, etc. Then the Shiny script can simply visualize that. And use cron or Windows Task Scheduler to make your download/calculation script run on regular intervals.

When the user opens the browser and points to http://serverIP:8100, what browser is that? IE8 and 9 are only supported when going through Shiny Server, not when Shiny apps are being served directly out of R (as in this case). Firefox, Chrome, Safari should all be OK though.

messages.subject: Re: How to determine data loading progress in Shiny?
messages.subject_clean: How to determine data loading progress in Shiny?
messages.body_plain:
Matthew, this could theoretically done (and doesn't need to be done in Shiny core) but the only way I can imagine it right now involves C, R, and JavaScript. Write a custom connection <http://biostatmatt.com/archives/2448> (in C) and sink() it before the operation begins; when the custom connection is written to, it would call session$sendCustomMessage in Shiny, and some JavaScript code would know how to display it to the user. If the progress messages involve txtProgressBar() then the JS code needs to get pretty involved. So, possible but would take some real effort on someone's part.

messages.subject: Re: conditionalPanel based on internal logic
messages.body_plain:
You absolutely can't do this:

fn1<-reactive({
  new<-paste(output$txt1,"again")
  new
})

In server.R, the output object can only have values set on it, they are not readable. If you want to reuse "hello" or whatever logic that is meant to stand in for, create a reactive expression that you use from both output$txt and fn1.

messages.subject: Re: loading *.dat - Files
messages.body_plain:
file<-reactive({
        inFile<-input$file
        if(is.null(inFile))
            return(NULL)
        load(inFile$datapath)

        output$file<-renderPlot({
            plot(file())
        })
    })

needs to be this:

    file<-reactive({
        inFile<-input$file
        if(is.null(inFile))
            return(NULL)
        load(inFile$datapath)

    })
    output$file<-renderPlot({
        plot(file())
    })

I also think that when you call load() you will need to pass in an envir argument explicitly.

messages.subject_clean: I updated to the latest version of shiny... an error now occurs... also: reactiveValues()
messages.body_plain:
What version of httpuv do you have installed?

For your second question, it depends entirely on how visible the "vars" variable is. If it's declared inside your shinyServer function, then it's unique to each session. If it's declared in global.R or the top of server.R, then it's shared by all sessions, and reactivity caused by one session will trigger changes in any other sessions that have a reactive dependency on it. See this article: http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#scoping

Note that these are all supported uses of reactivity; there's nothing wrong with having reactivity flow across sessions if that's what you want.

Because the "input" object is passed into your shinyServer function, it's specific to each session; a unique input and output object is created at the start of each session.

Does that answer your question?

messages.subject: Re: Please help! Plotting data after reading with renderTable
messages.subject_clean: Please help! Plotting data after reading with renderTable
messages.body_plain:
Hi Cyndy, the data reading operation should be extracted into a reactive expression. Then you access this data by calling the reactive expression as if it's a function.

Anytime you want to reuse the value generated by some logic, you should think "reactive expression".

    shinyServer(function(input, output) {

      filedata <- reactive({

        inFile <- input$file2
        if (is.null(inFile))
          return(NULL)
        return(
          read.csv(inFile$datapath, header=input$header, sep=input$sep, quote=input$quote)
        )

      })

      # You only need this if you have a tableOutput("contents") in your ui.R
      output$contents <- renderTable({
        filedata()
      })

      output$plot <- renderPlot({
        p <- qplot(filedata())
        print(p)
      })

- much faster

messages.body_plain:
There are a couple issues with this as a csv file:
* The fields appear to be separated with tabs, not commas.
* The "plot id" header should be in quotes to indicate that it's one item. Strings generally should be in quotes in a csv file, although some csv readers will accept non-quoted strings.
* There are four headers, but only three columns.

The csv file should look something like this (this is from R's built-in PlantGrowth dataset):
"weight","group"
4.17,"ctrl"
5.58,"ctrl"
5.18,"ctrl"
6.11,"ctrl"
4.41,"trt1"
3.59,"trt1"
5.87,"trt1"
3.83,"trt1"

-Winston

Thanks,
-Kevin

messages.body_plain:
This should be all you need. The content function is called at download time, so you don't need to worry about keeping it up-to-date.

Also, there's almost never a reason to assign an output from inside an observer. Nor to call renderImage without assigning it to an output slot.

output$downloadReport2<- downloadHandler(
    filename <- function() {
      paste(toupper(gsub("stock_","",input$variable)),'Sentiment', Sys.Date(),'.png',sep='')

      },

    content <- function(file) {

      png(file, width = 980, height = 400, units = "px", pointsize = 12,

         bg = "white", res = NA)

      make_chart(toupper(gsub("stock_","",input$variable)))

      dev.off()
    },
    contentType = 'image/png'
  )

messages.subject_clean: extracting data frm a Shiny object - splitting a csv read object
messages.body_plain:
If that split call is happening directly inside of your server function, and not inside another reactive() or a renderXXX call, then it's indeed wrong. You're asking to access mydata, which is reactive, but you're not running in a context that is itself reactive; put another way, you've asked for the value and to be notified about changes to the value in the future yet you've called it in a way that makes it impossible for you to be notified in the future.

In this case, if this error didn't exist, the call would succeed but the value would be NULL 100% of the time (since it occurs as the session is starting up, before the user has given us any input) and would never change from NULL.

So either make a new reactive expression that represents the split data [ datalist <- reactive(split(mydata(), mydata()$group)) ] or do the splitting directly in your renderPlot or whatever if you don't need that data from more than one place.

messages.subject: Re: FancyBox-like functionality / Invalidate a plot directly from JavaScript
messages.subject_clean: FancyBox-like functionality / Invalidate a plot directly from JavaScript
messages.body_plain:
That's a good idea but not something we have planned at the moment.

If you expand the div that contains a plot, call $(el).trigger('shown') and the plot will automatically redraw to the new dimensions. (This occurs unless the user specifies height and width arguments when calling renderPlot.)

To make it work with a new, expanded div would be tricky. You would need to unbind the old div and bind the new div. You can do this by calling Shiny.bindAll(container) and Shiny.unbindAll(container). Then when the fancybox is dismissed then you need to unbind the new div and bind the old div. Keep in mind that Shiny.bindAll and Shiny.unbindAll need to be called on the *container* of the .shiny-plot-output, not the .shiny-plot-output div itself. And this can be problematic if there are input/output elements that are siblings to the plot. I guess it would be useful to have a bindOne/unbindOne for this case but we don't have that today.

messages.subject: Re: Exposing dendrogram data to Javascript
messages.body_plain:
Gotcha.  I didn't know how to add additional parameters, each attempt just broke it, so instead I just changed the input to a list.  I just incorporated the existing color ranges functions from gplots.  For anyone who may be interested in changing the colors:

renderHeatmap <- function(expr, env = parent.frame(1), quoted = FALSE) {
  func <- shiny::exprToFunction(expr, env, quoted)

  function() {
    data <- func()[[1]]
col=func()[[2]]
    matrix <- as.matrix(data)

    rng <- range(matrix)

    #   rowClust <- hclust(dist(matrix))
    #   matrix <- matrix[rowClust$order,]
    #   colClust <- hclust(dist(t(matrix)))
    #   matrix <- matrix[,colClust$order]
    tmp <- tempfile()
    png(tmp)
    hm <- heatmap(data, keep.dendro=TRUE)
    dev.off()
    unlink(tmp)
    rowClust <- as.hclust(hm$Rowv)
    colClust <- as.hclust(hm$Colv)
    matrix <- matrix[hm$rowInd, hm$colInd]

    rowDend <- hclustToTree(rowClust)[[1]]
    colDend <- hclustToTree(colClust)[[1]]

    domain <- seq.int <http://seq.int>(rng[1], rng[2], length.out = 100)
    require(gplots)

        if (length(col) == 1 && is.character(col)){
        colz <- get(col, mode = "function")
    colors <- colz(100)
    colors <- sub('FF$', '', colors)
}

    matrix <- list(data = as.numeric(t(matrix)),
                   dim = dim(matrix),
                   rows = row.names(matrix),
                   cols = names(matrix),
                   colors = colors,
                   domain = domain)

    return(list(rows = rowDend, cols = colDend, matrix = matrix))
  }
}

#' @export
showHeatmap <- function(mat) {
  shiny::runApp(
    list(
      ui = basicPage(
        heatmapOutput('heatmap')
      ),
      server = function(input, output) {
        output$heatmap <- renderHeatmap(
          mat
        )
      }
    )
  )
}

On Wednesday, July 24, 2013 11:33:13 AM UTC-7, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> That's a good idea but not something we have planned at the moment.
>
> If you expand the div that contains a plot, call $(el).trigger('shown') and the plot will automatically redraw to the new dimensions. (This occurs unless the user specifies height and width arguments when calling renderPlot.)
>
> To make it work with a new, expanded div would be tricky. You would need to unbind the old div and bind the new div. You can do this by calling Shiny.bindAll(container) and Shiny.unbindAll(container). Then when the fancybox is dismissed then you need to unbind the new div and bind the old div. Keep in mind that Shiny.bindAll and Shiny.unbindAll need to be called on the *container* of the .shiny-plot-output, not the .shiny-plot-output div itself. And this can be problematic if there are input/output elements that are siblings to the plot. I guess it would be useful to have a bindOne/unbindOne for this case but we don't have that today.

messages.subject: Re: Is there a way to suppress 'events' during input to a field?
messages.subject_clean: Is there a way to suppress 'events' during input to a field?
messages.body_plain:
The reactive functions you use are updating instantly, because you did not isolate them:

instant update:

renderUI{(

   dosomethingwith(input$yourinput)

)}

patient update:

renderUI{(

   input$trigger.event (e.g. input$goButton)

   dosomethingwith(isolate(input$yourinput))

)}

With the first version the input$yourinputs get invalidated inside your renderUI as soon as is changes its value.
With the second version on the other hand input$yourinput does not force your renderUI into reactivity anymore, because it is isolated, meaning that renderUI grabs the current input$yourinput value only if it reacts to some other unisolated variable (like a button push event of so).

It took me some time get my head wrapped around to it, but once you got the concept, you can do cool stuff.
For example, I use it to dynamically set initial values of UI-elements like

numericInput("number1", value = ifselse(is.null(input$number1), 1, isolate(input$number1)))

You need this if you have a lot of reacitivity in you interface, so that html-divisions get rerendered constantly.

Hope it helps.

Ciao

messages.subject: Re: Exposing dendrogram data to Javascript
messages.body_plain:
Hey Joe,
I was able to get it up and running to an extent- but for an unknown reason it ceases to do so correctly after 'refreshing', being updated with new parameters.  After updating the heatmap, the values no longer display in the upper left (or anywhere), and the row/column labels no longer highlight.  Additionally, the previous dendrograms for the rows and columns persist, and overlap with the subsequent dendrograms.

here is the edited function I am using for the app:

 renderHeatmap <- function(expr, env = parent.frame(1), quoted = FALSE) {

  func <- exprToFunction(expr, env, quoted)

  function() {
    data <- func()[[1]]
col=func()[[2]]
    matrix <- as.matrix(data)

    rng <- range(matrix)

    #   rowClust <- hclust(dist(matrix))
    #   matrix <- matrix[rowClust$order,]
    #   colClust <- hclust(dist(t(matrix)))
    #   matrix <- matrix[,colClust$order]
    tmp <- tempfile()
    png(tmp)
    hm <- heatmap(data, keep.dendro=TRUE)
    dev.off()
    unlink(tmp)
    rowClust <- as.hclust(hm$Rowv)
    colClust <- as.hclust(hm$Colv)
    matrix <- matrix[hm$rowInd, hm$colInd]

    rowDend <- hclustToTree(rowClust)[[1]]
    colDend <- hclustToTree(colClust)[[1]]

    domain <- seq.int <http://seq.int>(rng[1], rng[2], length.out = 100)
    require(gplots)

        if (length(col) == 1 && is.character(col)){
        colz <- get(col, mode = "function")
    colors <- colz(100)
    colors <- sub('FF$', '', colors)
}

    matrix <- list(data = as.numeric(t(matrix)),
                   dim = dim(matrix),
                   rows = row.names(matrix),
                   cols = names(matrix),
                   colors = colors,
                   domain = domain)

    return(list(rows = rowDend, cols = colDend, matrix = matrix))
  }
}

messages.subject: Shiny, knitr and dynamic reporting
messages.body_plain:
I hope that with his topic an uncovered area will be more clearly defined. Lets say we have a shiny app with some ui.R (or www/index.html) and a server.R. Lets suppose that the shiny app has for simplicity two input textfields one for first name and one for last name of an individual. Consider that we have properly structured a .Rnw document that waits for some R to be injected. So the question is. How input$firstname and input$lastname would be passed in the .Rnw document so that knit2pdf() function will produce dynamically a report with each first name and last name that an individual types. And lastly , how the new download link will produced in server.R?

**i set this questions after i have written whatelse is marked under shiny and knitr

I think it is a very interesting part and i think that reactiveRnw() function should be a must have addition in next shiny release!

messages.subject: Re: Shiny, knitr and dynamic reporting
messages.body_plain:
Use downloadButton("report") in your ui.R, and on the server:

output$report <- downloadHandler(
  filename = "myreport.pdf",
  content = function(file) {
    knit2pdf("input.Rnw", file)
  },
  contentType = "application/pdf"
)

In your Rnw I *think* you should be able to simply refer to input$firstname and input$lastname directly.

messages.subject: Re: Linked Statistical Data Analysis
messages.body_plain:
I love this. Great work.

On Monday, July 22, 2013 11:58:43 AM UTC-5, Sarven Capadisli wrote:
> Hi all,
>
> I'd like to share a Shiny implementation.
>
> I created http://stats.270a.info/
>
> Paper/documentation on the whole thing at:
>
> http://csarven.ca/linked-statistical-data-analysis
>
> Basically the application utilizes federated SPARQL queries to gather
> statistical observation values from different endpoints based only on
> user's selections (independent, dependent variables, and reference
> period). The Shiny application and server bridges the front-end Web user
> interface with R on the server-side in order to compare statistical
> observations, and stores analysis results in RDF for future research.
>
> Source code at:
>
> https://github.com/csarven/lsd-analysis
>
>
> So, for instance, here is one analysis that's most likely not that
> interesting, but it will give you an idea on how it works:
>
> http://stats.270a.info/analysis/worldbank:SP.DYN.IMRT.IN/transparency:CPI2009/year:2009
>
> Independent variable from World Bank
> Dependent variable from Transparency International
> Reference period year 2009
>
> There is content negotiation going on for that URI, so if you are using
> your Web browser, you'll probably get the .html (regular web UI)
> serialization. However, if you requestion for RDF/XML, Turtle, or JSON,
> you'll get those serializations e.g.:
>
> curl -LH "Accept: application/rdf+xml"
> http://stats.270a.info/analysis/worDYN.IMRT.IN/transparency:CPI2009/year:2009
>
> Since there are way too many combinations, I don't pre-compute and store
> them. Instead, I let the users take care of that. Every analysis that's
> conducted is written to the RDF store. You can what was analysed so far:
>
> http://stats.270a.info/sparql?query=SELECT+*+WHERE+{+%3Fs+a+%3Chttp%3A%2F%2Fstats.270a.info%2Fvocab%23Analysis%3E+}%0D%0A%0D%0A&default-graph-uri=&output=xml&stylesheet=%2Fxml-to-html-links.xsl <http://stats.270a.info/sparql?query=SELECT+*+WHERE+%7B+%3Fs+a+%3Chttp%3A%2F%2Fstats.270a.info%2Fvocab%23Analysis%3E+%7D%0D%0A%0D%0A&default-graph-uri=&output=xml&stylesheet=%2Fxml-to-html-links.xsl>
>
>
>
> Currently, the application lets you select from the following Linked
> Datasets:
>
> * World Bank (only Indicators)
> * European Central Bank
> * OECD
> * FAO of UN
> * Transparency International
>
> It can be extended simply by adding more query endpoints.
>
> I plan to add IMF, BIS, and Eurostat soon.
>
> See also: http://270a.info/
>
>
> I still have *a lot* of things to iron out - I would only call this
> version 0.1 - but all feedback is most welcome!
>
> I'll follow up with bite size feedback and questions in separate emails.
>
> And, thanks again to everyone for helping me get through Shiny and
> server basics... well, still learning :)
>
> -Sarven
> http://csarven.ca/#i
>

messages.subject: Re: records
messages.body_plain:
hope i am not out of my place here,

but here is what i did

for (1), you can do something like this

  data_frame<-reactive({
    raw_data<-input$file1
    if(is.null(raw_data))
      return(NULL)
    read.csv(raw_data$datapath,header=TRUE,sep=",")
  })

and followed by another command that does something like

download<-reactive({
setwd("~/ShinyApps")
write.csv(data_frame(),"insert name.csv",row.names=FALSE)
})

however, the problem here you might then face is whenever a user uploads a data, the existing file will be over written, what i did to over come this problem is to create a log file.
you can think of this log file as a counter, so you can do something like

counter<-read.csv("counter.
csv",header=FALSE,sep=",")

and replace write.csv(data_frame(),"insert name.csv",row.names=FALSE) with

write.csv(data_frame(), paste("insert name.csv",counter),row.names=FALSE)

for 2)

R has a build in command for the time, which is

Sys.time(), you can play around with it. what i did was

time<-as.character(Sys.time())

and also append it in my log file.

for  IP address, there are some people asking about it a long time ago, its quite complicated ( i didnt bother to read them as i dont require them as of now)

as for the other settings, when you define them as reactive functions, you can append them in your log file. its up to you as to how you want to design your log file and play with it.

just remember to write.csv for your counter file again after adding +1 to it.

i hope this helps

messages.subject: Re: records
messages.body_plain:
To record IP address requires the very latest version of Shiny (i.e. install directly from GitHub, instructions are at https://github.com/rstudio/shiny) as well as the very latest version of httpuv. Updating httpuv is actually a little complicated; you need to have Rtools installed if you're on Windows, and you need git. If you have both of those, then you should be able to do:

git clone https://github.com/rstudio/httpuv
cd httpuv
git submodule update --init
R CMD INSTALL .

You can then include a "session" argument in your shinyServer function (i.e. function(input, output, session)) and then refer to session$request$REMOTE_ADDR to get the client IP address. If you're running behind Shiny Server you will need to get the value a different way, take a look at session$request$HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR (see here <http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-Forwarded-For> for more details).

messages.subject: Re: throttling redraws when up/down-ing a numericInput
messages.subject_clean: throttling redraws when up/down-ing a numericInput
messages.body_plain:
There's no built-in way to do custom throttling at the moment. But you could fake it on the server side like this (assume the thing we want to throttle is called input$number):

values <- reactiveValues()
observe({
  invalidateLater(500)
  values$number <- isolate(input$number)
})

Then everywhere you would refer to input$number, refer to values$number instead. Reactivity shouldn't be fired if values$number is assigned the same value that it already is, so the effect of this is to only fire reactivity when something has changed and then only once every 500 millis.

messages.body_plain:
If the overwriting is happening inside the reactive expression, it should be fine. If not... you'd have to explain a little more about how/when the rewriting happens for me to answer definitively. Ok, so I did a little experimentation and found this:

If I update one of the timestamps in that data object "allData", the update works fine, however I notice that when I try to save the new timestamp (or anything else) to the allData object, it doesn't actually save it.  I had it print the timestamp to the console for me and noticed that the timestamp would always be the same as the original timestamp even after updating it.  Essentially, if the global allData object is modified by the reactive function, the allData object doesn't get saved in its modified version, it just stays the same as the original value it had when it was loaded.

If I print out the output of the reactive function itself, I see the updated timestamp.

Why is it that I can't modify the global allData object from within the reactive function?  Should I be setting allData = reactiveFunction()?

On Tuesday, July 30, 2013 10:18:10 AM UTC-6, Trevor Paulsen wrote:

> Basically the data object is a combination of many hundreds of API calls stitched together which takes a long time to assemble by itself.  When a user accesses my Shiny page, I'm fetching only incremental updates to the data based on a timestamp.  When I use the returned data object from the reactive function, the data is updated correctly, however when it runs a second time it's as if the updated timestamp never happened and it runs the same update over again.
>
> I've included the data as a global object.  Do any changes I make to that global object in a reactive function show up to all other output functions?  Do I have to use the output of the reactive function, or can I just call it and use the updated global object?

> On Mon, Jul 29, 2013 at 6:20 PM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:

> > If the overwriting is happening inside the reactive expression, it should be fine. If not... you'd have to explain a little more about how/when the rewriting happens for me to answer definitively. Ideally you would not overwrite sub-objects of a giant object, but simply create new reactive expressions; unless there is a good reason for these things to be glommed together into one giant object, you'll get better performance and more understandable code by just keeping separate things separate.

To set a variable that's in a parent environment, you need to use the <<- operator instead of <- or =.

For example:
x <- 1
f <- function() {
  x <- 2
}
f()

x
# 1

g <- function() {
  x <<- 3
}
g()
x
# 3

-Winston

>                    step=10)
>     ),
>     mainPanel(
>       plotOutput("parameterPlot")
>     )
>   )
> )
and the server:
> library(shiny)
>
> options(digits.secs=3)
>
> default.parameter <- 50
> min.invalidate <- 10
> max.invalidate <- 5000
> t1 <- .5
> t2A <- .25
> t2B <- .5
> tmax <- 3
>
> clip.validate <- function(x) min(max.invalidate,max(min.invalidate,x))
>
> shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
>   vInput <- reactiveValues()
>   vInput$oldParameter <- default.parameter
>   vInput$state <- 0
>
>   wInput <- reactiveValues()
>   wInput$parameter <- default.parameter
>
>   observe({
>     if ((vInput$state == 0)&&
>         (vInput$oldParameter != input$parameter)) {
>       vInput$state <- 1
>       vInput$oldParameter <- input$parameter

>       invalidateLater(clip.validate(t1*1000),session)

>     if ((vInput$state > 0)&&

>     if ((vInput$state == 2)&&
>         (as.numeric(Sys.time())>vInput$wakeupTime)) {
>           vInput$state <- 0
>           wInput$parameter <- input$parameter
>     } else {
>     if ((vInput$state == 2)&&

>           vInput$oldParameter <- input$parameter
>           vInput$wakeupTime <- as.numeric(Sys.time())+t2B

>     if ((vInput$state > 0)&&

messages.subject: Re: Validating UI controls
messages.body_plain:
Inside the reactive/output function, start off with
if(!is.numeric(input$submittedStuff))
return() # don't run further if this has characters
if(nchar(input$submittedStuff)==0)
return() # don't run further if it is empty

and in separate text output$warnings, you can use similar checks to see if it should display text warning of improper input, or return() and not show any warnings if it's all good.

That's how I went about similar issues.

messages.subject: Making input object accessible to R session for debugging help?
messages.subject_clean: Making input object accessible to R session for debugging help?
messages.body_plain:
I've recently really started playing more with Shiny and love it. One aspect of extreme frustration is, as you probably know, tracking down bugs or oddities in the code. One thing that would make this *unbelievably* easier would be to somehow make the input object available in the current R session. This way, I could run the code in server.R in my session without having to re-define everything taking an input$var value.

Is there any way to do this? Hopefully what I'm suggesting is clear?

ui.R
==========

sliderInput(inputId = "var1", label = "var1",
                min = 0, max = 50, value = c(10, 25), step = 5),

sliderInput(inputId = "var2", label = "var2",
                min = 0, max = 50, value = c(10, 25), step = 5),
...
==========

server.R
==========

lapply(something, function (x) {
  expand.grid(seq(min(input$var1), max(input$var1), length.out = 10),
    seq(min(input$var2), max(input$var2), length.out = 10)),
    ...
 } )
==========

Silly example, but imaging having something go awry with lapply() (common for me). Now I need to execute it manually and replace every instance of input$soemthing with a real value.

Is there a way to automate this, or perhaps I don't understand debugging shiny apps at all and am going about this all wrong. I read the run & debug bit on the tutorial, but I don't think that's what I want. I'm new enough to R that just seeing the error message isn't going to help me. I end up wanting to see the results of head() or str() on an object created in the app, but I can't get to it since it's only running in shiny, not the session. Thus, I have to manually recreate an analog to my shiny code in the session itself, and run into the issue of replacing all my references to input$.

Thanks,
John

messages.subject_clean: throttling redraws when up/down-ing a numericInput
messages.body_plain:
Gah, that's a fairly terrifying amount of state-mutating code--I'd be worried about its correctness.

If you're comfortable in JavaScript, the other option is to create your own custom input binding that forks what we do in shiny.js and overrides getRatePolicy.

See https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/inst/www/shared/shiny.js#L1187 for an example; keyup and input events have 250ms debounce applied, while change event causes an immediate update.

On Tue, Jul 30, 2013 at 4:06 PM, David Gonzales <dvdgon...@gmail.com> wrote:
> PS
> I forgot to mention I also patched the shiny.js at one point, but that should apply to typing values manually in the numericInput. this test is mainly to get the up/down value changes to be more gentle with redrawing.
>
>
> On Wednesday, July 31, 2013 2:01:39 AM UTC+3, David Gonzales wrote:
> > I have a simple version of my responsiveness investigation.
> > I am posting the code here (will figure out later how to host it publicly):
> > > library(shiny)
> > >
> > > default.parameter <- 50
> > >
> > > shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
> > >   headerPanel("Reactiveness test"),
> > >     sidebarPanel(
> > >       numericInput("parameter",

> > >     )
> > >   )

> > > library(shiny)
> > >
> > > options(digits.secs=3)
> > >
> > > default.parameter <- 50
> > > min.invalidate <- 10
> > > max.invalidate <- 5000
> > > t1 <- .5
> > > t2A <- .25
> > > t2B <- .5
> > > tmax <- 3
> > >
> > > clip.validate <- function(x) min(max.invalidate,max(min.invalidate,x))
> > >
> > > shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
> > >   vInput <- reactiveValues()
> > >   vInput$oldParameter <- default.parameter
> > >   vInput$state <- 0
> > >
> > >   wInput <- reactiveValues()
> > >   wInput$parameter <- default.parameter
> > >
> > >   observe({
> > >     if ((vInput$state == 0)&&
> > >         (vInput$oldParameter != input$parameter)) {
> > >       vInput$state <- 1
> > >       vInput$oldParameter <- input$parameter
> > >       vInput$wakeupTime <- as.numeric(Sys.time())+t1
> > >       vInput$maxTime <- as.numeric(Sys.time())+tmax
> > >       invalidateLater(clip.validate(t1*1000),session)
> > >     } else {
> > >     if ((vInput$state > 0)&&
> > >         (as.numeric(Sys.time())>vInput$maxTime)) {
> > >       vInput$state <- 0
> > >       wInput$parameter <- input$parameter
> > >       invalidateLater(clip.validate(t2A*1000),session)
> > >     } else {
> > >     if ((vInput$state == 1)&&
> > >         (vInput$oldParameter != input$parameter)) {
> > >       vInput$state <- 2
> > >       vInput$oldParameter <- input$parameter
> > >       vInput$wakeupTime <- as.numeric(Sys.time())+t2B
> > >       invalidateLater(clip.validate(t2B*1000),session)
> > >     } else {
> > >     if ((vInput$state == 1)&&
> > >         (as.numeric(Sys.time())>vInput$wakeupTime)) {
> > >       vInput$state <- 2
> > >       vInput$wakeupTime <- as.numeric(Sys.time())+t2A
> > >       invalidateLater(clip.validate(t2A*1000),session)
> > >     } else {
> > >     if ((vInput$state == 2)&&
> > >         (as.numeric(Sys.time())>vInput$wakeupTime)) {
> > >           vInput$state <- 0
> > >           wInput$parameter <- input$parameter
> > >     } else {
> > >     if ((vInput$state == 2)&&
> > >         (vInput$oldParameter != input$parameter)) {
> > >           vInput$oldParameter <- input$parameter
> > >           vInput$wakeupTime <- as.numeric(Sys.time())+t2B
> > >           invalidateLater(clip.validate(t2B*1000),session)
> > >     }}}}}}
> > >     if ((vInput$state > 0)&&
> > >           (as.numeric(Sys.time())<=vInput$wakeupTime)) {
> > >       invalidateLater(clip.validate((vInput$wakeupTime-as.numeric(Sys.time()))*1000),session)
> > >     }
> > >   })
> > >
> > >   output$parameterPlot <- renderPlot({
> > >     data <- rnorm(100000,mean=wInput$parameter)
> > >     hist(data,xlim=c(0,100))
> > >   })
> > > })
> >
> > what do you think about this behavior?
> >
> >
> > On Wednesday, July 31, 2013 12:39:02 AM UTC+3, Andrew Clark wrote:
